explanation: He bade that Paul be examined by scourging, that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

question: What did Paul ask the centurion as they bound him with thongs?
choices: Whether it is lawful to scourge a Roman uncondemned
Whether he could speak to Caesar
Whether he could send a letter
explanation: Paul said, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

question: Who went and told the chief captain to take heed because Paul was a Roman?
explanation: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

question: Why was the chief captain afraid when he learned Paul was a Roman?
explanation: The chief captain was afraid, after he knew that Paul was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

question: Whom did Paul name as witnesses to the letters he received to go to Damascus?
choices: The high priest and all the estate of the elders
explanation: Paul said the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders, from whom he received letters.

question: About what time of day did the great light shine round Paul?
explanation: As Paul was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light.

question: What did Paul ask the Lord after he learned the voice was Jesus of Nazareth?
explanation: Paul said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord told him to arise and go into Damascus.

question: What title did Ananias give Jesus when he said Paul would see him?
explanation: Ananias said God chose Paul to know his will, and see that Just One, and hear the voice of his mouth.

question: What did Ananias say Paul should be doing as he was baptized and washed his sins away?
choices: Calling on the name of the Lord
explanation: Ananias said, Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

question: According to what was Paul taught at the feet of Gamaliel?
choices: The perfect manner of the law of the fathers
The sayings of the prophets only
explanation: Paul was taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God.

question: Who gave Ananias a good report, according to Paul?
choices: All the Jews which dwelt there
explanation: Ananias was a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there.

question: With what was Paul bound when he told the centurion he was a Roman?
explanation: As they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman?

question: What did the chief captain say he paid to obtain his freedom as a Roman?
explanation: The chief captain said, With a great sum obtained I this freedom.

question: What did Paul answer the chief captain about his own citizenship?
choices: It was given me by Caesar
explanation: Paul said, But I was free born.

question: How did Paul address the crowd when he began his defence?
explanation: Paul began, Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.

question: What did the men who were about to examine Paul do when they heard he was a Roman?
explanation: Straightway they departed from him which should have examined him.

question: What did the chief captain ask Paul when the centurion warned him?
choices: Tell me, art thou a Roman?
explanation: The chief captain said, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

question: What did the voice say to Paul on the road when he fell to the ground?
choices: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
Saul, rise and stand upon thy feet
explanation: Paul fell unto the ground and heard a voice saying, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

question: What did Ananias say the God of our fathers had chosen Paul to know?
explanation: Ananias said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will.

question: What did Paul call the high priest when he was told to be struck on the mouth?
explanation: Paul said, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall.

question: What did Paul cry out that he was when he saw the council was part Sadducees and part Pharisees?
choices: A Sadducee, the son of a Sadducee
A Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee
explanation: Paul cried out, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee.

question: What did the chief captain fear would happen to Paul in the council?
choices: That he would be pulled in pieces
That he would be stoned at once
explanation: The chief captain feared lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, and commanded the soldiers to take him by force.

question: In which city did the Lord say Paul must bear witness, as he had in Jerusalem?
explanation: The Lord said, As thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

question: What did the Jews who banded together swear not to do until they had killed Paul?
explanation: They bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

question: Which two groups in the council became divided over Paul?
explanation: There arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.

question: To which city did the soldiers bring Paul to the governor?
explanation: When they came to Caesarea, they delivered the epistle to the governor, and presented Paul also before him.

question: Who wrote the letter to Felix about Paul?
explanation: The letter began, Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

question: Where did Felix command that Paul be kept?
explanation: Felix commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.

question: What did the chief captain command the soldiers to do when the dissension grew great?
choices: Take Paul by force and bring him into the castle
explanation: He commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

question: Why did Paul rebuke Ananias for commanding him to be smitten?
choices: Ananias sat to judge him by the law yet broke the law
explanation: Paul said, Sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

question: What did Paul say when told he was reviling God's high priest?
choices: I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest
I spoke the truth before God
explanation: Paul said, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest.

question: What did the Sadducees say there is not?
explanation: The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

question: What did the scribes of the Pharisees' part say they found in Paul?
explanation: The scribes of the Pharisees' part said, We find no evil in this man.

question: What did the Lord say Paul had done in Jerusalem?
explanation: The Lord said, As thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

question: How many men made the conspiracy to kill Paul?
explanation: They were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

question: To whom did the conspirators go with their plan to kill Paul?
explanation: They came to the chief priests and elders and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse.

question: What reason were the council to give the chief captain for bringing Paul down?
choices: To enquire something more perfectly concerning him
explanation: They said to signify to the chief captain to bring him down, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him.

question: What did Paul ask a centurion to do for the young man?
choices: Bring him to the chief captain
explanation: Paul said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

question: How did the chief captain treat the young man when he came?
choices: Took him by the hand and went aside privately
explanation: The chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him what he had to tell.

question: What did the chief captain charge the young man to do?
choices: Tell no man what he had shown
explanation: The chief captain charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

question: What did Lysias say in his letter when he rescued Paul?
choices: He understood Paul was a Roman
explanation: Lysias wrote that he came with an army and rescued Paul, having understood that he was a Roman.

question: What did Lysias write that Paul had nothing laid to his charge worthy of?
explanation: Lysias perceived Paul to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

question: Which province did Felix learn Paul was from?
explanation: When Felix read the letter, he asked of what province Paul was, and understood that he was of Cilicia.

question: What did Felix say he would do when Paul's accusers were also come?
explanation: Felix said, I will hear thee, when thine accusers are also come.

question: What Scripture did Paul quote when he said he did not know Ananias was the high priest?
choices: Thou shalt not bear false witness
Honour thy father and thy mother
Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people
Thou shalt not strike the Lord's anointed
explanation: Paul said, It is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

question: What did those standing by say to Paul after he answered Ananias?
choices: Hast thou no fear of Caesar?
explanation: They that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest?

question: What were the forty men waiting for from the chief captain?
explanation: They said they were ready, looking for a promise from thee.

question: Where did Paul's sister's son go to tell Paul of the ambush?
explanation: When Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

question: How many soldiers did the chief captain order made ready to go to Caesarea?
explanation: He said, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred.

question: How many horsemen were ordered to go with Paul?
explanation: The chief captain ordered horsemen threescore and ten to go with the soldiers.

question: At what hour of the night were the soldiers to leave?
explanation: They were to go to Caesarea at the third hour of the night.

question: What did the chief captain say to provide for Paul's journey?
explanation: He said, Provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

question: What did Lysias say he came with when he rescued Paul?
explanation: Lysias wrote that Paul should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him.

question: Of what did Lysias say Paul was accused?
explanation: Lysias perceived Paul to be accused of questions of their law.

question: What did Lysias say he commanded Paul's accusers to do?
choices: Say before Felix what they had against him
explanation: Lysias gave commandment to his accusers also to say before Felix what they had against him.

question: Where did the soldiers bring Paul by night on the first stage of the journey?
explanation: The soldiers took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

question: Who went on with Paul to Caesarea on the next day?
explanation: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle.

question: Where did Lysias say he brought Paul to learn why they accused him?
explanation: Lysias wrote that when he would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, he brought him forth into their council.

question: When did the Lord stand by Paul and bid him be of good cheer?
explanation: The night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul.
